props.gloss_en: Rav and Shmuel: anything that has of the five species in it -- over it one says 'Who creates kinds of food'
it was also stated, Rav and Shmuel both said: anything that is of the five species -- over it one says 'Who creates kinds of food'
had he taught only 'anything that is', I would say [mezonot] because it is in its own form, but in a mixture not; so he taught 'anything that has in it'
and had he taught only 'anything that has in it', I would say that rice and millet in their own form also get 'Who creates kinds of food'; so he taught 'anything that is'
only over what is of the five species does one say 'Who creates kinds of food' -- excluding rice and millet, over which even in their own form one does not
if they brought before him rice bread or millet bread, he blesses over it at the start and at the end, like a cooked dish
of a cooked dish it was taught: at the start one says 'Who creates kinds of food'
and at the end one blessing abridged from the three
like a cooked dish and not like one: blessings before and after, but here, at the start, 'by Whose word all things came to be'
and at the end 'Who creates many living things and their needs, for all that You have created'
these are cooked dishes: split kernels, teraggis, flour, zariz, arsan -- and rice
whose is this [list]? It is R' Yochanan ben Nuri's
R' Yochanan ben Nuri: rice is a species of grain -- one is liable to karet for its leavening, and a person discharges his obligation [of matza] with it on Pesach
but the Rabbis -- no
one who chews wheat says 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
ground, baked and cooked, while the slices are intact: at the start 'Who brings forth bread from the earth', and at the end three blessings
if the slices are not intact: at the start 'Who creates kinds of food', and at the end one blessing abridged from the three
and one who chews rice says 'Who creates fruit of the ground'
[rice] ground, baked and cooked, even though the slices are intact: at the start 'Who creates kinds of food'
and at the end one blessing abridged from the three
whose is it? If you say R' Yochanan ben Nuri's, who said rice is a species of grain
rather, is it not the Rabbis'?
